@graph.headline: Options Trading Charges in India (2026): The Complete Cost Breakdown With a Real Worked Trade
@graph.description: How much does an options trade really cost in India? STT, brokerage, exchange fees, GST and stamp duty explained with a rupee-by-rupee NIFTY trade example.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to trade one NIFTY options lot in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Buying and selling one NIFTY option lot at a ₹100 premium (lot size 65) costs roughly ₹63 in total charges — ₹26.49 on the buy leg and ₹36.04 on the sell leg. That is about ₹0.96 per share just to get in and out. The option must move in your favour by at least that much before you have made a single rupee of profit.

mainEntity.name: Do I pay STT when buying options?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. STT (Securities Transaction Tax) on options is charged only when you sell — 0.15% of the premium, effective 1 April 2026. There is no STT on the buy leg. The mirror image is stamp duty: 0.003% of premium turnover, charged on the buy side only.

mainEntity.name: What is STT on options trading in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two rates apply. On the sale of an option, STT is 0.15% of the premium (raised from 0.10% on 1 April 2026). On an exercised option, STT is 0.15% of the intrinsic value, paid by the purchaser. If the option expires worthless, there is no exercise and no exercise STT. These are government rates — identical at every broker.

mainEntity.name: Which trading charges are the same at every broker?

acceptedAnswer.text: Almost everything except brokerage. STT, exchange transaction charges (0.03553% of premium on NSE), the SEBI turnover fee (₹10 per crore), stamp duty, and GST (18% on brokerage + exchange + SEBI charges) are set by the government, exchanges, and regulators — your broker cannot change them. Only the brokerage itself varies: the discount-broker norm is a flat ~₹20 per executed order.

mainEntity.name: What happens to charges if I let my option expire?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the option expires out of the money, it expires worthless — no sale leg, so no sale STT and no brokerage on exit. If it expires in the money and is exercised, STT of 0.15% applies on the intrinsic value, paid by the option holder.

mainEntity.name: Do intraday and positional option trades pay different charges?

acceptedAnswer.text: The charge structure is identical — same brokerage, same STT, same exchange and regulatory charges. What differs is the holding cost: positional trades may face overnight margin requirements, and any option held into expiry faces the exercise-STT question.
